Two matter day to day: codex queue --resume and codex doctor --network-only . Both are flags on existing commands, so knowing what each command already does is the quickest way to see what changed. articles.excerpt: HuskHoard Active Archive for Dummies: Building an "Infinite" File Server Have you ever wished your computer had a hard drive that simply never filled up? What if you could store 100 Terabytes of video…
articles.body: HuskHoard Active Archive for Dummies: Building an "Infinite" File Server Have you ever wished your computer had a hard drive that simply never filled up? What if you could store 100 Terabytes of video files, backups, and documents, but only pay for a 2 Terabyte high-speed NVMe drive? Welcome to the world of the Active Archive . In traditional storage, a file is either "alive" on your fast server or "dead" in cold storage (like a dusty USB drive or an offsite cloud backup). An Active Archive (powered by HuskHoard) bridges this gap. It creates the illusion of infinite, instantly accessible high-speed storage while quietly doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes. Here is the step-by-step guide to exactly how this magic works.

articles.title: Property Management Email 429 Rate Limit Handling for Contact Routing
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Handle email API 429 rate limit errors at a durable queue boundary: honor Retry-After, retry with bounded jitter, and keep the property-management queue and idempotency key unchanged. A…
articles.body: Short answer: Handle email API 429 rate limit errors at a durable queue boundary: honor Retry-After , retry with bounded jitter, and keep the property-management queue and idempotency key unchanged. A 429 from an email API should pause delivery at the queue boundary, not trigger an immediate retry in every request handler. For a property-management contact form, keep the selected support queue and an idempotency key in durable storage, honor Retry-After when present, and retry with bounded exponential backoff plus jitter. The form request should acknowledge accepted work only after that record exists. This ordering matters because a tenant asking about a leaking roof should reach maintenance, while a lease question belongs with leasing.

articles.title: Ignition vs ICONICS GENESIS: one license per server or five license tiers
articles.excerpt: Inductive Automation's Ignition and ICONICS GENESIS (version 11, the successor to GENESIS64) are both full HMI/SCADA platforms that now market unlimited licensing. They get there differently: Ignition…
articles.body: Inductive Automation's Ignition and ICONICS GENESIS (version 11, the successor to GENESIS64) are both full HMI/SCADA platforms that now market unlimited licensing. They get there differently: Ignition sells one perpetual license per server and publishes its prices, while GENESIS uses five license tiers and runs on a Windows, IIS and SQL Server stack. Licensing model Ignition : one license per server. Standard licenses are perpetual (one-time); Cloud Edition is usage-based. GENESIS : five tiers, Pure, Plus, Professional, Prime and Platinum. All licenses on one network must be the same tier. Tags and clients Ignition includes unlimited tags, unlimited clients and unlimited concurrent Designers per server license.

articles.body: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable ’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962.

Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

Colors of the Moon Explanation: What color is the Moon? It depends on the night — and the time. Outside of the Earth’s atmosphere , the dark Moon , which shines by reflected sunlight, appears a magnificent ly brown-tinged gray. The featured image highlights a collection of apparent colors of the full moon on Earth, documented by one astrophotographer over 10 years from different locations across Italy .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
